newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon expects to add 100 jobs in Mass.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon expects to add 100 jobs in Mass.

text.p: Raytheon Electronic Systems, which won a federal contract that ultimately could be worth as much as $1 billion, expects to hire at least 100 more people at its Marlborough, Massachusetts, office to do the work.
The Raytheon Co unit will be the prime contractor for a Federal Aviation Administration system called STARS -- the Standard Terminal Automation Replacement System.

While the new contract is not expected to create jobs at one of Raytheon's key team members, Sun Microsystems, another firm, Hughes Electronics Corp, does see limited job gains, most likely in Massachusetts.
"We anticipate hiring 10 to 20 people in the Boston area, who will be co-located with Raytheon, the prime contractor," said John Shea, a spokesman for Hughes.
He added, "We don't see any appreciable hiring in the near-term out in Fullerton, California," where the Hughes unit that will be handling other parts of the task is located.

Raytheon, which has about 16,000 employees in Massachusetts, making it one of the state's biggest employers, is planning on expanding its engineering and design office in Marlborough, which is located about 30 miles west of Boston.
"We estimate that this contract award will probably create in excess of 100 engineering and technical support jobs," said Gail Haze, a company spokeswoman.
In contrast, the new contract, which will replace aging terminals with an open system, is not expected to oblige Sun to add staff.

"We're not going to be required to hire additional people to meet these requirements," said John Leehy, a spokesman for Sun Federal, a Washington-based unit of Sun Microsystems. --Joan Gralla, 212-859-1654
